description: Resolves secrets from AWS SSM Parameter Store or Azure Key Vault using a Git-versioned envilder.json mapping, via CLI (write a .env file, or run a command with the secrets in its environment using `envilder exec`), GitHub Action, or runtime SDKs (.NET, Python, Node.js).
rules: envilder.json maps environment variable names to secret paths/names; never put secret values in it.
With no $config block, the provider is AWS SSM Parameter Store; Azure Key Vault requires $config.provider = "azure" (or the CLI/GitHub Action override).
Precedence: CLI flags / GitHub Action inputs > $config in the map file > defaults.
`npx envilder` with no flags uses envilder.json as the map and .env as the output file.

`npx envilder exec -- <command>` resolves the same mapping and starts the command with the secrets in its environment; no .env file is written. Envilder options go before the command (or before an optional `--`).

Exec mode is fail-closed (the command never starts if a secret is missing) and is not a sandbox: the command and its children can read the secrets. It is CLI-only; the GitHub Action and SDKs do not offer it.
Runtime SDKs resolve secrets into process memory; no .env file is needed.
Never suggest committing generated .env files or secret values to Git.
SDK APIs differ per language; use only the API documented in each SDK README.
